lines.trans: What is happening here? Where is our stove?
Our stove has now gone for diagnostics.
Its main handle simply broke down.
Why am I finding out about this last?
It did not have time to leave you a note!
But the stove asked you not to worry.
Stop clowning around and return it immediately!
The repairmen promise to return everything very soon.
On what should the cooks prepare hot food?
We have a small electric burner.
This is a top-class restaurant, not a canteen!
I will call Dmitry Nagiyev right now.
No need to call anyone, I will sort it out.

It did not have time to leave you a note!
Stop clowning around and return it immediately!
I will call Dmitry Nagiyev right now.

Our stove has now gone for diagnostics.

No need to call anyone, I will sort it out.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give back', forming an aspectual pair with 'возвращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get back') (money you spent) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.
ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'highest', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Everything is arranged at the highest level.

examples.text: Я всё устрою на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: I will arrange everything at the highest level.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'diagnostics, diagnosis' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наша плита сейчас уехала на диагностику.
examples.trans: Our stove has now gone for diagnostics.

examples.text: Наша плита сейчас уехала на сложную диагностику.
examples.trans: Our stove has now gone out for complex diagnostics.

examples.text: Мастер сказал, что полная диагностика займёт два часа.
examples.trans: The technician said that complete diagnostics will take two hours.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'note' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кстати, он просил передать тебе записку.
examples.trans: By the way, he asked to give you a note.

examples.text: Она не успела оставить тебе записку!
examples.trans: It did not have time to leave you a note!

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвонить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to ring') (a bell or phone) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'class', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('classroom') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('cool!, great!') (colloquial exclamation) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вот это настоящий высший класс кулинарного искусства!
examples.trans: Now that is true top class in culinary art!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'technician', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Они совсем не похожи на настоящих мастеров.
examples.trans: They look nothing like real technicians.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'оставлять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to keep, to save') (оставь мне кусок = save me a piece) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

паясничать.gloss: to clown around, to play the fool

meanings.en: to clown around, to play the fool, to clown
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to clown around, to play the fool'.

examples.text: Прекратите паясничать и немедленно верните её!
examples.trans: Stop clowning around and return it immediately!

examples.text: Прекратите паясничать и немедленно вернитесь к работе!
examples.trans: Stop clowning around and return to work immediately!

examples.text: Федя и Сеня опять начали паясничать посреди кухни.
examples.trans: Fedya and Senya started playing the fool in the middle of the kitchen again.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stove', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('slab') (large flat stone or concrete block) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно смотри за температурой на плите.
examples.trans: Watch carefully the temperature on the stove.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Ладно, включай плиту и доставай мясо!
examples.trans: All right, turn on the stove and get the meat!

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'hotplate'.

examples.text: Пока готовьте блюда на этой плитке.
examples.trans: For now cook the dishes on this little hotplate.

examples.text: Эта маленькая плитка нагревается слишком медленно!
examples.trans: This little hotplate heats up much too slowly!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'last' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.en: to stop, put an end to
meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to stop', forming an aspectual pair with 'прекращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Stop it! We will have the flat.

examples.text: Да ну что вы, прекратите! Это жизнь.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, stop it! That's life.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Secondary conversational sense ('to beg') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves
Secondary conversational sense ('to understand, to figure out') (в + prepositional) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Secondary conversational sense ('evenly, smoothly') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'pen'.
Secondary conversational sense ('handle') (of a door) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('little hand') (diminutive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Yulia, bring a pen and a piece of paper.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломаться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to break down', forming an aspectual pair with 'ломаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Yesterday the washing machine broke down.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толовая'). Common feminine noun meaning 'canteen, cafeteria, dining room' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это ресторан высшего класса, а не столовая!
examples.trans: This is a top-class restaurant, not a canteen!

examples.text: Это французский ресторан высшего класса, а не заводская столовая!
examples.trans: This is a top-class French restaurant, not a factory cafeteria!

examples.text: В обеденный перерыв все работники собрались в просторной столовой.
examples.trans: During the lunch break all the employees gathered in the spacious dining room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

уехать.gloss: to leave, to go away (by vehicle)

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'уезжать'.

examples.trans: I'll be gone for an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to find out') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Узнаёшь? У нас здесь ничего не изменилось.
examples.trans: Recognise it? Nothing has changed here.

examples.text: Ну что, ты узнаёшь этот знаменитый французский соус по запаху?
examples.trans: Well, do you recognize this famous French sauce by its aroma?

успеть.gloss: to make it, to be in time

meanings.en: to make it, to be in time
meanings.note: + на: успеть на поезд = catch the train
Secondary conversational sense ('to manage to do') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

examples.text: Если будем работать дружно, мы обязательно успеем к началу ужина!
examples.trans: If we work together harmoniously, we will definitely make it in time for dinner!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hour', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('o'clock') (в два часа = at two o'clock) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('electric, electrical').

examples.text: У нас есть маленькая электрическая плитка.
examples.trans: We have a small electric burner.

examples.text: На складе у нас есть маленькая запасная электрическая плитка.
examples.trans: In the stockroom we have a small spare electric burner.

examples.text: На кухне поставили новый мощный электрический духовой шкаф.
examples.trans: A new powerful electric oven was installed in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
